Definition: The parts of a program that a person sees and interacts with, like windows, buttons, and lists.
One part of a user interface that a person can interact with, like a button, a checkbox, or a text field.
A Quorum class that opens a window for an app. A Form holds one or more Pages.
One screen of a Form. You add controls to a Page, and the Form shows one Page at a time.
A Quorum class that opens a window and draws the screen many times a second. Controls can be added to a Game, next to pictures and animation.
A class with the code that runs when something happens, such as a button being pressed.
The control that keyboard input goes to right now. Only one control has the focus at a time.
When an interface changes its arrangement to fit the size of the screen or window it is shown on, such as moving a label above its field on a narrow screen.
A program that reads the screen aloud or sends it to a braille display, used by people who are blind or have low vision.
The field that studies how people use computers and how to design technology that works well for them.
